title: Visitor and Choir
premise: Ulyana Dravenmoor returns to the frost-bound town of Vesper Hollow to bury their twin sister Vera, only to discover the body in the casket is wearing Ulyana's face. The old photographs of grandma's house keep gaining an extra chair at the table, and each new chair pulls Ulyana deeper into a founding ritual the town's ancestors left unfinished — a bargain that demands one twin be given to the frost so the other may live. As the winter deepens and the townspeople's polite smiles curdle into complicity, Ulyana uncovers that their grandmother was the last to refuse the ritual, and that justice here was never written into law but into ice. In the climax, Ulyana chooses to finish the founders' rite backwards, offering the truth instead of a body, unmasking the town's elders as the true sacrifice; the frost takes them, the extra chair empties, and Ulyana leaves Vesper Hollow carrying Vera's memory home at last.
about_author: Z. M. Reyes is the pen name of a former small-town archivist who spent years cataloguing funeral records and family photographs in rural northern communities. Their fiction blends folk horror with quiet domestic dread, exploring what families agree never to say aloud.

chapters.title: The Wrong Face in the Casket
chapters.summary: Ulyana arrives in Vesper Hollow for Vera's funeral and lifts the coffin lid to find their own face staring back. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: grief curdling into vertigo as the town watches too calmly.

chapters.title: Grandma's House Keeps Its Appointments
chapters.summary: Ulyana stays at the decaying family house and hears footsteps upstairs matching Vera's old gait. A neighbor, Mrs. Aldous, warns them not to unpack. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: denial hardening into vigilance.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Explanations
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: teenage Ulyana and Vera's final fight before Vera fled town, and the first unexplained noise grandma dismissed. POV: alternating past/present Ulyana. Emotional beat: guilt over the last words they exchanged.

chapters.title: An Extra Chair
chapters.summary: Sorting grandma's photo albums, Ulyana finds every picture of the dining room now contains a ninth chair, pulled to the table's center, though the room holds eight. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: rational explanations begin to fail.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: In the church basement archive, Ulyana finds a ledger listing founding families and a column headed 'Given,' with Dravenmoor entered twice — once for 1847, once blank and waiting. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: dread of inherited obligation.

chapters.title: Polite People, Locked Doors
chapters.summary: The town hosts a condolence dinner where no one will say Vera's name and everyone asks whether Ulyana is 'staying through the frost.' Sheriff Brannic escorts them home. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening into paranoia.

chapters.title: What Vera Left in the Walls
chapters.summary: Ulyana pries open a sealed closet and finds Vera's journals: she'd been researching the ritual for years and believed the frost chose its own vessel. POV: mostly Vera via journal excerpts, framed by Ulyana. Emotional beat: posthumous reconciliation beginning.

chapters.title: The Chair Moves Closer
chapters.summary: New photographs develop on their own in grandma's darkroom; in each, the extra chair sits nearer the camera until it faces the viewer directly. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the horror turns personal — the chair is an invitation.

chapters.title: Mrs. Aldous Confesses Half of It
chapters.summary: The elderly neighbor reveals her own brother was Given in 1974 and that the town's prosperity — its unbroken harvests, its absence of crime — is purchased annually. POV: Mrs. Aldous, then Ulyana. Emotional beat: pity entangled with complicity.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Ulyana digs into county records: every official who investigated disappearances resigned, retired rich, or vanished. The law was bought generations ago. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: rage replacing fear; resolve forming.

chapters.title: The Frost Writes First
chapters.summary: Overnight, frost patterns bloom across Ulyana's windows spelling out the ledger's blank entry: DRAVENMOOR. The house temperature drops and won't rise. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the deadline becomes physical.

chapters.title: Twin Sense
chapters.summary: Ulyana begins dreaming Vera's memories — her research, her terror, her final night in the founder's chapel beneath the church. POV: dream-Vera bleeding into Ulyana. Emotional beat: love against duty; Ulyana refuses to accept Vera is gone.

chapters.title: The Chapel Beneath
chapters.summary: Following the journals, Ulyana finds a hidden stair from the crypt to a round chamber with nine alcoves and a central empty dais shaped like a chair. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: awe and revulsion at the ritual's architecture.

chapters.title: The Choir That Isn't Singing
chapters.summary: Sunday service: the congregation sings a hymn whose melody matches the hum Ulyana has heard in the walls. Mid-verse, the choir falls silent in unison and all turn toward the back pew. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: communal menace made explicit.

chapters.title: Brannic's Offer
chapters.summary: Sheriff Brannic privately offers Ulyana a way out: leave tonight, renounce the name, and the town will 'find another way.' Ulyana realizes the alternative vessel would be Mrs. Aldous's grandniece, a child. POV: dual Ulyana/Brannic. Emotional beat: temptation versus conscience.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Ulyana burns the ledger page bearing their name; by morning the frost has rewritten it, and the photographs now show two chairs at the table's center. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: defiance met with escalation; despair's floor drops out.

chapters.title: The Night of the Long Frost
chapters.summary: The coldest night in recorded history seals the roads. Townsfolk gather at the church carrying lanterns, singing the silent hymn, escorting Ulyana gently — horribly gently — toward the crypt. POV: rotating townsfolk then Ulyana. Emotional beat: horror of kindness weaponized.

chapters.title: The Ninth Chair Is Warm
chapters.summary: In the chapel, the founders' descendants reveal the rite's final step: the Given must sit willingly, or the frost takes the whole town — including the child. Ulyana sees Vera's outline seated in the eighth alcove, waiting. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the choice distilled to its cruelest form.

chapters.title: Reading the Rite Backwards
chapters.summary: Remembering Vera's marginal note — 'a bargain read backwards is a confession' — Ulyana sits not in the ninth chair but on the dais itself and speaks the founders' names as accusation rather than invocation. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: courage as refusal.

chapters.title: What the Ice Remembers
chapters.summary: The frost abandons the ledger and writes the founders' crimes across every window in town; the eldest descendants age decades in minutes as the debt reverts to its original signers. POV: multiple witnesses, then Ulyana. Emotional beat: terrible justice, finally outside any law but honest.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Grave
chapters.summary: Ulyana reburials the casket under both twins' names, and Vera's presence — footsteps, warmth, a final dream goodbye — fades with the thaw. Mrs. Aldous's grandniece is safe; the town must live with what it did. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into release.

chapters.title: Leaving Before the Next Winter
chapters.summary: Ulyana packs the photographs — the extra chair gone from every one except the last, where it stands pushed back, empty, like a seat kept for a guest who chose to leave. On the road out, frost ferns bloom briefly on the windshield, shaped like a wave. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: bittersweet departure; the past acknowledged, not escaped.
